source: US Dam Hazard Classification - Corrected Edition (2026-11-09), Appendix A; In-Depth Summaries: Dam & Pond Hazard Classification - Federal Agencies and the States (Nov. 2026)
dash_rule: A dash in the document (no confirmed method) falls back to M13 and engineering judgment; a preset with no confirmed scenario must have one chosen by the user (flagged).
aliases_note: Alternate preset IDs accepted everywhere a preset ID is (resolve_preset, hand-off validation, screener PRESET, damit:classify PRESET_ID). Each alias maps to one stored ID; a run records the stored ID.

status_values.unverified: The source document marks the preset's governing wording (Unverified); confirm before relying on it.
status_values.draft: The governing guidance is itself marked DRAFT in the source document.

status_note: A preset 'status' marks the whole preset (its governing document), not a method: the methods it uses stay as documented in methods.json. Method-level marks for one preset go in the preset's 'verification' map (e.g. BIA M5 secondary).

FEMA333.label: FEMA 333 baseline
FEMA333.notes: Summaries F-1: classification reflects incremental consequences of failure or misoperation, never condition or likelihood; loss of an occasional recreational user or passer-by is improbable (R1); no credit for evacuation or EAPs (R3).

USBR.label: USBR (ACER TM-11)
USBR.citation: USBR ACER TM-11 (Dec. 1988, MDE-hosted); Graham (1999) DSO-99-06

conditional_scenarios.source: Summaries F-3: sunny-day default, stepped flood-plus-failure comparison for borderline dams

USBR.notes: M1 marks the lives in jeopardy (habitable structures in the high-danger zone) that M5 counts (TM-11: 1-6 Significant, more than 6 High); M1 returns no class by itself (class_zones empty). Summaries F-3: the five depth-velocity charts are used to assess lives in jeopardy; the 1-6 / >6 bands are 'purely arbitrary' (TM-11). S5 for borderline dams was (unverified) in the Corrected Edition and is stated without a mark in the Summaries.

BIA.label: BIA
BIA.citation: FEMA P-919 (July 2012) summary of BIA practice (secondary); CRS R45981
BIA.notes: Summaries F-8 / Part III: 1-6 lives at risk Significant, more than 6 High (TM-11 bands). The source also says Significant covers 'significant property damage' and that 'any dam creating a hazard to human life' is High; neither clause has its own M-code here, so they need engineering judgment.

NRCS.label: NRCS
NRCS.notes: NRCS hazard-definition wording (NEM § 520.21) is (unverified) in the Corrected Edition. The Summaries F-2 report § 520.21 verified verbatim (High: 'may cause loss of life or serious damage to homes, industrial or commercial buildings, important public utilities, main highways, or railroads'; TR-210-60 reads 'industrial and commercial'; both read 'township and country roads'). The 'unverified' status is kept pending the owner's decision. Classification considers existing and future downstream development (R5).
NRCS.status_review: Summaries F-2 marks NEM § 520.21 verified; status kept 'unverified' (owner decision 2026-11-09).

ND.label: North Dakota (REG_05.2026)
ND.citation: N.D.A.C. § 89-08-01-01 (amended Jan. 1, 2015; Jan. 1, 2023; July 1, 2024); DWR policy REG_05.2026 § 5 (eff. April 1, 2026); N.D.C.C. § 61-03-25 (EAPs); DWR June 2023 release
ND.notes: REG_05.2026 supersedes REG_05.2024a. 'Significant' means the same as 'Medium'. Modal verbs kept as written: M6 'may' and R4 'should' are advisory. The simplified (no-breach-model) option is § 5.1.2; REG_05.2026 § 5.5 cites a non-existent '§ 5.1.3' (an error in the policy, flagged, not propagated). EAPs: N.D.C.C. § 61-03-25 (not the repealed 89-08-04-03).

NE.label: Nebraska
NE.citation: NeDNR / DWEE Classification of Dams (Dec. 2023) Table 3, §§ 2.2, 2.32, 2.35; Title 458; Neb. Rev. Stat. § 46-1601 et seq. (§ 46-1618 defines hazard potential classification)
NE.notes: Agency: Department of Water, Energy, and Environment (DWEE) since July 1, 2025 (LB317). Table 3 rows (homes, institutions, industrial / commercial, campgrounds, roads, railroads, utilities, environmental losses) re-checked against the Summaries S-7: unchanged. M4a stays advisory ('should', Appendix A).

NY.label: New York
NY.notes: DOW TOGS 3.1.5 is still marked DRAFT (Summaries S-8). M5 (High at 1+ life): TOGS 3.1.5 'where loss of a single human life is likely, ... a high hazard (Class C) dam is implied' (both source documents; not in the Appendix A.6 bundle). Owners may contest a class with an engineer's analysis.

VA.label: Virginia
VA.citation: 4VAC50-20-40, -45, -52, -54 (amended eff. Jan. 14, 2026; Va. Reg. Vol. 42 Iss. 9); Va. Code § 10.1-604 et seq.
VA.notes: S1 + S5 = four analyses (sunny day; SDF with and without failure; PMF with failure).

TX.label: Texas
TX.citation: 30 TAC § 299.14; 30 TAC § 299.1 (as amended eff. Sept. 29, 2022); Tex. Water Code § 12.052(e-1); TCEQ GI-394; SAO 20-036
TX.notes: 30 TAC § 299.14 classifies on 'either potential loss of human life or property damage': M4c (1-6 lives or 1-2 habitable structures Significant; 7+ lives or 3+ habitable structures High) and M13 Texas wording for the economic-loss half (Summaries S-10: appreciable economic loss - isolated homes, secondary highways, minor railroads, interruption of public utilities - Significant; excessive economic loss in or near urban areas High). A breach analysis may address the incremental impact over the flood causing the breach (permissive; no S-code confirmed). The § 12.052(e-1) exemption and § 299.1 jurisdiction are not classification rules.

ID.label: Idaho
ID.citation: IDAPA 37.03.06 Rule 25; IDWR Dam Safety Program

CO.label: Colorado
CO.notes: Rule 4.13 (renumbered from Rule 4.2.14). The 'designated recreational sites' sentence in some secondary sources is superseded Rule 4.2.14.1 text and is not used.

CA.label: California
CA.scenario_note: Sunny-day loading (the document does not map it to a specific S-code; choose S1 or S2 explicitly).

AK.label: Alaska
AK.citation: 11 AAC 93.157 (as amended Oct. 2, 2004); 5 AAC 95.011(a) for M12c
AK.notes: Class II anadromous-fish criterion is 11 AAC 93.157(a)(2)(D): probable damage to waters identified under 5 AAC 95.011(a) as important for the spawning, rearing, or migration of anadromous fish. The older 'salmon spawning habitat as identified by the Commissioner of Fish & Game' wording (ASDSO 2020) is superseded and not used. M13 uses the 11 AAC 93.157 Class II / III wording (Summaries S-2); Class II also names a significant health hazard potential, which an engineer checks.

AL.label: Alabama
AL.citation: Ala. Code §§ 33-7-71 to -74 as amended by SB 378 (2026; Act 2026-482 per bill trackers, secondary); SB 284 (Act No. 2023-414)
AL.notes: Summaries S-1: High / Significant / Low (FEMA-style). The sources give no Alabama-specific criteria, so M5 (High at 1+ life) and M13 are the FEMA 333 defaults and the run is flagged for engineering judgment. Program administered by the Alabama Emergency Management Agency (AEMA); changes effective October 1, 2026; participation is voluntary for private dam owners; AEMA's implementation plan is due by the 15th day of the 2027 session. The act number (2026-482) is confirmed only by bill trackers (secondary) and the exact signing day is unpublished.

NC.label: North Carolina
NC.notes: Summaries S-12 (spot-verified): Class A (low) / B (intermediate) / C (high), FEMA-aligned. No North Carolina-specific criteria in the sources: M5 (High at 1+ life) and M13 are the FEMA 333 defaults (flagged). The small-dam exemption (under 50 ac-ft unless failure could result in loss of human life or significant damage to property below the dam) is a jurisdiction rule, not a class rule, and is not encoded; its pinpoint (.0102 vs .0105) is an open item.

USACE.label: USACE (FEMA 333 terminology)
USACE.citation: USACE Dam Safety Program; FEMA P-919 summary of USACE incremental analysis; CRS R46946 / R45981
USACE.notes: Summaries F-4: FEMA 333 terminology for NID hazard fields; incremental consequence analysis with loss of life as the controlling criterion (economic damage expressly not the driver). The Corrected Edition marks this (secondary). No separate numeric matrix: M5 (High at 1+ life) with M13 for the FEMA 333 Low / Significant terms (flagged). DSAC is portfolio risk prioritization, not hazard classification; EM 1110-2-1420 (hydrologic engineering) is not a class rule.

TVA.label: TVA (FEMA 333 tiers)
TVA.notes: Summaries F-9: TVA self-regulates and its disclosures classify on FEMA 333 tiers: Low = no lives at risk, flood wave contained on TVA property; High = one or more lives. M5 (High at 1+ life); Significant is not defined in the sources beyond the FEMA 333 tier, so M13 is the fallback (flagged).

no_preset.FERC: Summaries F-5: risk-informed consequence assessment (Engineering Guidelines Ch. 2 hazard potential and IDF selection; Ch. 18 Level 2 risk analysis); population at risk and warning time drive life-safety consequences. The sources state no class tiers or desk-screen thresholds, so no method bundle.
no_preset.USFWS: Summaries F-6: 361 FW 2 defines hazard classification (potential loss of life or property damage; not condition) and classifies by hazard and size, but gives no class tiers or thresholds.
no_preset.MSHA: Summaries F-7: Low / Significant / High under 30 CFR 77.216 and 56/57.20010 'based on potential damage', with hazard creep; the sources give no tier criteria to encode.
no_preset.OTHER_STATES: Summaries S-12: the remaining ~40 states follow FEMA 333 with state-specific guidance; no per-state rules are in the sources, so they use an agency preset (e.g. FEMA333) or custom mode.

no_preset_note: Agencies and states the source documents cover without a classification rule that can be written as a method bundle. Listed so the gap is documented, not filled with invented rules.
